name: Katowice Wojciech Korfanty International Airport
before:
Poland's fourth busiest airport, at Pyrzowice 30 km north of Katowice, with just under 7.3 million passengers in 2025. More usefully for a tour operator, it is the largest source of charter flights in the country and second for cargo.

The terminal split is unusual and worth explaining. Terminal A handles non-Schengen departures, Terminal B handles Schengen departures and Terminal C takes all arrivals, whichever they came from. Between them they are rated for about 8 million passengers a year, with an expansion announced in 2024 aiming at 12 million by 2028.

The runway is 3,200 metres, the second longest in Poland after Warsaw, and takes aircraft up to a 747 or 777 though not at maximum weight. Antonov An-124s have landed here on occasion.

Wizz Air bases aircraft here and services its A321neo fleet on site, with Linetech maintaining Embraer E190s.

Two things for the enthusiast: the control tower is the tallest in Poland and Eastern Europe at 46 metres, and there are two free plane spotting stands.
after:
Poland's fourth busiest airport, at Pyrzowice, 30 km north of Katowice. It handled just under 7.3 million passengers in 2025, its first year above 7 million.

There are three terminals, and the arrivals hall is in Terminal C. The runway is 3,200 metres long.
